_comment: Notification-hook surface: every priority critical|high entry whose last_changed_at falls in the last 7 days, most recently changed first. last_changed_at = max(discovered_at, every non-internal updates[].at): it moves on a new finding AND on every reader-facing update, correction or improvement (updated_at moves only on a type:update record). Poll this file and alert on a new `id` OR a changed `last_changed_at` for a known id. `immediate_action` is non-null exactly when priority is critical. URLs are absolute (`url` == `permalink`; `markdown_url` is the entry's raw Markdown source). Schema: {id, url, permalink, markdown_url, priority, kind, headline, summary, discovered_at, updated_at|null, last_changed_at, updates[{at,type,summary}], immediate_action:{title,action}|null, actions[], exploited, kev, cve_ids[], cves[{id,cvss|null,status[],affected|null,fixed|null}], affected_products[], entities[], techniques[], tags[], sectors[], regions[], verification, classification|null, org_triage:{category,rationale}|null}. exploited = an exploitation tag or a CVE status of exploited/cisa-kev; kev = a CVE on the CISA KEV list. techniques[] carries the entry's MITRE ATT&CK ids (frontmatter + prose-derived, revoked ids resolved forward); classification is the collapsed Admiralty code (e.g. B2). For the do-now task list of every priority, poll data/actions.json. See docs/pipeline.md.

alerts.summary: Drupal published SA-CORE-2026-017 (CVE-2026-132165) and SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166, Moderately critical, not directly exploitable) on 2026-11-18 and SA-CORE-2026-019 (CVE-2026-136716, Highly critical 21 of 25) on 2026-11-25: under specific conditions an attacker can use the installer to reinstall Drupal, which can lead to site takeover or remote code execution, and sites in unusual or incomplete install states stay open after the first fix. Drupal says both installer flaws are exploited on live sites (SA-CORE-2026-017 from 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC) and CISA listed CVE-2026-132165 as exploited on 2026-11-24; the fixed releases are 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23, update.php must be run, and securing the installer is strongly recommended.

Drupal revised SA-CORE-2026-017 to Highly critical (20 of 25, exploit status Exploit) and reports exploitation of CVE-2026-132165 on live sites from 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC; the fixed releases and the installer workaround are unchanged.

Drupal published SA-CORE-2026-019 on 2026-11-25 (CVE-2026-136716, Highly critical 21 of 25), a second installer flaw under which sites in unusual or incomplete install states stay open after the first fix, exploited in the wild according to Drupal; the fixed releases move to 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23 and update.php must be run. alerts.headline: nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update to 1.31.10, 1.30.8, Plus 37.3.1.1
alerts.summary: F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The memory-corruption fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, nginx 1.31.10, 1.30.8 and NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 add a fix for one CPU-exhaustion flaw, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings; Unit 42 reached pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the worker user in a lab, on a non-default configuration and with a separate memory leak that F5 has not given a CVE. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Veeam lists its 13.1 Software and Infrastructure Appliances (fixed through Veeam Updater), Cisco lists Catalyst Center, Identity Services Engine 3.5, Nexus 3000 and 9000 in standalone NX-OS mode, UCS Director and about 20 other products with fixes dated November 2026 to March 2027 or still to be determined, Siemens and Synology list products with fixes pending or none, and Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiMail, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM not impacted while 29 product names, FortiAuthenticator among them, remain under investigation.

updates.summary: Four vendors published product impact for the nginx flaws: Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled (three fixed builds out, three due 2026-11-23, HTTP/2 off as workaround), Cisco lists NX-OS and ISE 3.5 among affected products, Siemens Industrial Edge has no fix, and Fortinet is still investigating. None reports exploitation.

Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.1, moves UCS Director to affected and adds Unified Contact Center Express, Finesse and other products with fixes dated November 2026 to February 2027 or still to be determined; Synology lists DSM as affected with fixed builds for 7.4 and 7.3; Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy and FortiMail not impacted while 51 product names stay under investigation; and Ubuntu publishes USN-9159-1.

Siemens lists five Industrial Edge device products as affected, with Industrial Edge Hub and the Management products not affected; Rapid7 says only that its exploit runs with the nginx worker's permissions.

nginx.org and Fortinet list ten flaws fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7, five more than the entry's five: a TLS 1.3 request-body infinite loop rated major, an SNI bypass of client certificate validation in the stream module, a stream ssl_preread validation flaw, an alias and try_files buffer overflow, and a PROXY protocol version 2 NULL dereference in the 1.31 mainline; the fixed releases and the update action are unchanged.

Unit 42 reached pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the worker user in a two-VM lab, on a non-default configuration and chained with a memory leak F5 has not given a CVE, and publishes the exposure test and a log signal. Palo Alto Networks released its last three PAN-OS fixed builds and cleared 11.1 and 10.2, and Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.5, rates the flaws High and changes several product statuses and fixed releases.

nginx 1.31.10 and 1.30.8 (2026-11-23) and NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 fix a further flaw, CPU exhaustion when ssl_early_data is on (CVE-2026-132779), so the update target moves; Veeam lists its 13.1 Software and Infrastructure Appliances as affected by the two HTTP/2 flaws with a fix through Veeam Updater since 2026-11-25, and GitLab's Linux package carries nginx 1.31.9.

Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.6 of 2026-11-27, also lists Crosswork Hierarchical Controller, Secure Endpoint Private Cloud Appliance, Intersight, UCS Fabric Interconnect and Optical Network Controller and no longer names NextFusion Platform; Fortinet now clears FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM as well, keeps 29 product names under investigation and says it remediated FortiVoice Cloud and FortiEdge Cloud; Synology's revisions updated APM's fix status to 2.0.2-88107.

alerts.headline: GeoServer RCE chain: public PoC, CISA lists two flaws as exploited; update to 3.0.2, 2.28.6 or 2.27.7
alerts.summary: The GeoServer project published a batch of security advisories on 2026-11-23, most for flaws fixed in 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7, and five of them chain an anonymous WFS request to code execution: a path disclosure, a service-security bypass with a prefixed service name, an XML injection, a predictable remember-me key that forges an administrator session (critical, CVSS 4.0 9.2) and a JDBC deserialization. The reporter, who says it works on a default installation, published a full-chain proof of concept the same day; the project announced the fixed releases on 2026-10-19. CISA added CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-27 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe, watchTowr reports exploitation attempts in the form of error-based probes that create and invoke stored queries, and NCSC Switzerland rates the chain actively exploited.

updates.summary: watchTowr reports exploitation attempts against the GeoServer chain, in the form of error-based probes that create and invoke stored queries, and NCSC Switzerland rates the chain actively exploited; watchTowr is the only observer and the sources name different CVEs as exploited. The record also adds CVE-2026-120704, the SQLite JDBC extension-loading step that Eye Security's variant of the chain uses.

CISA added CVE-2026-120705 (XML injection) and CVE-2026-129243 (service-level authorization bypass) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-27 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe; the exploited status of the other three chain flaws still rests on watchTowr, whose table and prose differ.

alerts.headline: BACS: five confirmed AI-agent attacks in Switzerland, three on critical infrastructure; critical updates within 24 hours
alerts.summary: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cyber Security (BACS) said on 2026-11-24 that it had for the first time received reports of attacks on Swiss companies and critical-infrastructure operators in at least two sectors that were carried out with the support of an AI agent; on 2026-11-26 its director told SRF that BACS has five confirmed cases, three on critical-infrastructure operators, and SRF reports that systems were compromised in four of the five (RTS reads two successes among three critical-infrastructure attacks, and BACS's page says every case known on 2026-11-24). No framework, sector, victim or entry point is named for the Swiss cases and the actor is unknown; BACS says the number of internet-reachable agents such as ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI has almost doubled since October 2026 and recommends critical updates on internet-reachable systems within 24 hours.

updates.summary: BACS director Florian Schütz told SRF on 2026-11-26 that BACS has five confirmed cases of attacks with AI agents, three on critical-infrastructure operators, and SRF reports compromises in four of the five, while RTS reads two successes among three critical-infrastructure attacks and BACS's own page says every case known on 2026-11-24. actions: Patch CVE-2026-46300 on every Linux host that runs PHP or other internet-facing code, then on multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners: apply the distribution kernel update and reboot; until then, where IPsec is not in use, block and unload the `esp4`, `esp6` and `rxrpc` modules (this breaks IPsec), and drop the page cache so a file already modified in memory reloads from disk.

On any PHP web host, appliance or management server that was reachable and unpatched for the PHP2Shell flaws, look for PHP files in web-reachable directories that nobody deployed, an outbound SSH session from the host that a systemd service or an rc.local entry keeps up, and password-spray bursts against Active Directory from the host's address, because Dream Research reports a chain of the two flaws that did exactly that.
alerts.headline: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia): CISA lists the Linux kernel root flaw as exploited, chained with PHP2Shell
alerts.summary: CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", CVSS 7.8) is a local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel's xfrm ESP-in-TCP path, one of three CVEs Red Hat groups as "Dirty Frag"; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, and Dream Research reports such a chain against 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and a US government-affiliated network. Its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels are affected (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28 · Dream Research, 2026-10-29 · Red Hat RHSB-2026-003).

updates.summary: CVE-2026-46300's CVSS score has now been published (7.8) and Red Hat's own bulletin confirms RHEL kernels are affected (unlike sibling CVE-2026-43500, which Red Hat states does not affect its products). Public proof-of-concept exploits now target Kubernetes specifically, and Red Hat's bulletin groups this CVE under the collective "Dirty Frag" name alongside CVE-2026-43284/CVE-2026-43500, confirming the ESP-in-TCP exploitation path this entry already described and the coalescing-marker root cause are the same flaw.

The CVSS 7.8 figure came from the MITRE CVE record rather than from a cited advisory. It now cites Red Hat's CVE page, which publishes the same 7.8 score, and an evidence quote taken from the MITRE record is removed. The main text and action now carry the sourced interim mitigation (block esp4, esp6 and rxrpc, or disable unprivileged user namespaces) and the sourced patch status and discovery credits. Unsupported module names, a CAP_NET_ADMIN restriction, a kernel version range, wider patch coverage and a leftover table of three unrelated CVEs are removed, as is an unrelated actor link. The 2026-09-05 section now attributes the 7.8 score to Red Hat and cites Aikido for its container and detection guidance, which no longer says a module listing confirms IPsec use.

Aikido's statement that working Kubernetes proof-of-concept exploits have been published concerns the Dirty Frag family as a whole, not CVE-2026-46300 specifically; the summary and the 2026-09-05 section now attribute it that way, and no source describes a Kubernetes exploit for this CVE. Detection and triage lines are added from Wiz's description of the public exploit and Red Hat's list of legitimate user-namespace uses.

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root; Dream Research describes such a chain used against 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and a US government-affiliated network. The CVE record moves to exploited, the priority from notable to high, and the earlier statement that no source reports exploitation of this CVE is replaced. Removed from the text: the sentence that an attacker can modify any file the user can read (the Detection line still carries it) and, from the summary, the clause on Aikido's report of working Kubernetes exploits for the Dirty Frag family.

Dream Research's updated report names Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS as the product in the chain that paired the PHP2Shell flaws with this kernel flaw, and counts 25 rooted PAN-OS firewall and management servers; Unit 42 says it independently verified the tooling and results.

Dream's report, as updated on 2026-10-29, names the rooted firewalls as PAN-OS, so the 2026-10-29 section now does too and gives Dream's account of what the Active Directory attacks confirmed; the Exposure and takeaway lines now name PAN-OS management interfaces and Palo Alto's fixes. The CISA catalog statement is given in CISA's words, the root-step sentence follows Wiz's wording, and two at-disclosure sentences (Microsoft's no-exploitation statement, which the KEV listing superseded, and the early patch note) are removed.

Palo Alto's bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 (2026-11-24) says exploitation of CVE-2026-46300 has been observed against internet-exposed management interfaces, the vendor's own statement beside CISA's listing and Dream Research's account, and lists a first fixed PAN-OS build for the flaw in every train that is later than the PHP2Shell hotfix.

alerts.headline: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, 3.3.14 fix seven memory flaws; Veria's Rails exploit not found yet: update the interpreter
alerts.summary: The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 for seven memory-corruption flaws in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, three rated Critical, and says it knows of proofs of concept that reach remote code execution. Veria Labs, which found the case-conversion flaw independently (CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte heap overflow), says Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed without authentication in their default configuration and announced a code-execution proof of concept on stock Rails for 25 November 2026, which its page, blog feed and GitHub organisation did not show as released on 2026-11-27; no exploitation is reported. GitHub Enterprise Server and older GitLab branches now carry the fix. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life, and the interpreter itself, not a gem, must be updated.

actions: Copy the application and network logs of every self-hosted Zammad instance, then upgrade it to Zammad 7.2.3, the critical security update of 2026-11-11 that supersedes 7.2.2, and add the Remote-User header-clearing line next to X-Forwarded-User in its nginx or Apache2 configuration (the Docker images apply it automatically); a 6.5 instance that cannot be upgraded yet gets the 6.5.5 emergency fix from Zammad's new 6.5 package repository, and an older instance that cannot be upgraded goes offline.

On every instance that was internet-reachable on 6.3.0 to 6.5.4 since 2026-09-21, run DIVD's log-check script, and treat a hit, or any DEB or RPM host where code ran as the zammad account, as compromised, rotating every credential its database held (mail-channel passwords, OAuth client secrets and refresh tokens, API tokens) and revoking cloud OAuth tokens as well as isolating the host, because DIVD's forensic report shows the attacker read those tables and network isolation does not revoke tokens.

alerts.summary: DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. NCSC-NL states both have been exploited since 21 September and CISA listed both in KEV on 2026-10-02; Zammad says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older, and Horizon3 published the root cause and a working exploit for it on 2026-10-07. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, Zammad 7.2.3 of 2026-11-11, a critical security update, supersedes it, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited. DIVD's forensic report of 2026-11-25 says the attacker likely used ARTEX and moved from the Zammad host to Jira and Confluence by ARP poisoning and forged administrator session tokens.

updates.summary: CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalog on 2026-10-02, and Zammad's own statement of 2026-10-01 says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older (which receive no security fixes), that 7.0 and later are not affected and 7.2.0 hardens the code, and that it cannot confirm the root-escalation flaw because DIVD gave it no technical details. Zammad also says it first received a report about the code-execution flaw in August 2026, before the exploitation DIVD dates to 2026-09-21.

Zammad's own advisory of 2026-10-05 says it now has DIVD's technical details for CVE-2026-102490, assesses it as a local escalation that needs prior access to the server, ties it to a confirmed vulnerability in packager.io and is working on a solution; no fix is named yet. Zammad advises restricting access to the underlying server to trusted administrators.

Zammad released 7.2.1 on 2026-10-06 with 27 security advisories, two rated critical (a public sign-up path to other customers' tickets and a multi-factor bypass in the email-verification flow), all affecting 7.2.0 and earlier; 7.2.0 is therefore no longer the release to install. None of the advisories carries a CVE id, none is reported exploited, and no source says whether 7.2.1 fixes the exploited root escalation CVE-2026-102490.

Horizon3 published the root cause of CVE-2026-102489 and a working exploit on 2026-10-07: a single unauthenticated WebSocket request makes Zammad return an error carrying every active user's session cookies, and a leaked administrator session writes a mail template through the package installation endpoint that runs code as the zammad user. The exploited flaw now has a public exploit, and Horizon3 says the root escalation remains unpatched.

Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the local escalation from the zammad account to root that no vendor fix covered before, in DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations only; installations from source and the official container images were never affected. The exploited code-execution flaw and its public exploit are unchanged.

Zammad shipped 6.5.5 on 2026-10-15, an emergency release for the unsupported 6.5 series that hardens the WebSocket server code against the exploited code-execution flaw CVE-2026-102489; it installs only from a new package repository and does not extend 6.5 support. Zammad still tells every self-hosted installation to upgrade to 7.2.2, and the 6.5.5 notes do not mention the root escalation.

DIVD completed its forensic investigation: the attacker, who used AI agents after reaching root, was mainly after credentials (a GitLab token, a Slack key and shared-mailbox OAuth tokens); about 41,000 ticket titles and a limited set of older conversations left the host, and the first response started 19 hours after the alert. Zammad's release 7.2.3 of 2026-11-11, a critical security update, supersedes 7.2.2 as the build to install.

DIVD's forensic report of 2026-11-25 says the attacker likely used ARTEX and moved from the Zammad host to Jira and Confluence by ARP poisoning an unencrypted database link and forging administrator session tokens, took credentials from Zammad's database, and kept cloud OAuth access after network isolation. The alert fired 7 h 21 min before a volunteer looked at it and 19 h 23 min before the CISO was informed; containment finished 27 h 41 min after it.

alerts.headline: PAN-OS management interfaces rooted via PHP2Shell and a kernel flaw, both exploited per Palo Alto: hotfix, then check
alerts.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory, first published on 2026-10-21 and revised since, says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and Dream Research, with Unit 42's verification, reports a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw that rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and went on to attack a US government-affiliated Active Directory. The advisory lists every release below the hotfix for its train, of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama, as affected through the management web interface by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS-B 9.2); all twenty hotfixes are released, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. Palo Alto's bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 of 2026-11-24 says exploitation of that kernel flaw has been observed against internet-exposed management interfaces and lists a later hotfix per train that fixes it. A device that was exposed and unpatched needs a compromise check as well as the hotfix, and CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.

updates.summary: Palo Alto Networks' revised advisory now also lists the WildFire appliances WF-500 and WF-500-B as affected by the PHP flaws in all versions, schedules hotfix builds of every PAN-OS train between 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-30, and leaves Panorama and WF-500 undated; Cortex XCORE (SaaS) and WildFire Cloud are already remediated.

Palo Alto Networks' advisory now lists the WildFire appliances WF-500 and WF-500-B as unaffected, a correction its timeline dates 2026-10-23, has no separate Panorama row while a note keeps Panorama in scope, and extends the Threat Prevention coverage; the PAN-OS hotfix dates of 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30 and the exploitation statement are unchanged.

Dream Research's report, updated 2026-10-29, names Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS as the product behind the chain it had first described with an unnamed vendor: a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers and was followed by an attack on a US government-affiliated Active Directory, and Unit 42 says it independently verified the tooling and results. alerts.headline: Mitel MiCollab AWV flaws exploited pre-advisory per Accenture APEX, CISA lists them; patching alone does not evict
alerts.summary: Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0012 of 2026-11-16, revised on 2026-11-24 to list the CVE ids, covers five flaws in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier, led by an unauthenticated blind command injection scored CVSS 3.1 10.0 (CVE-2026-133323) and an unauthenticated XML injection scored 9.0 that could run commands (CVE-2026-133303). CISA added all five to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without naming an actor, victim or technique, while Mitel's own page says nothing on attacks; Accenture APEX Labs reports exploitation before Mitel's 2026-11-16 advisory, with web-shell activity at one victim before 23:00 UTC on 2026-11-15 and root within about 30 minutes, so a server patched now cannot be assumed clean. Mitel offers a patch through its portal (KB000129195) and says restricting external access to the AWV component reduces the risk; the 10.3.0.18 release that Mitel named as the fix for its July advisory is itself in the affected range.

updates.summary: MITRE assigned CVE ids to all five flaws on 2026-11-19: CVE-2026-133323 for the CVSS 10.0 command injection and CVE-2026-133303 for the 9.0 XML injection, with CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133311 and CVE-2026-133324 for the three medium flaws. Mitel's advisory page still lists only its own tracking ids.

CISA added all five MiCollab AWV flaws, among them the unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 command injection, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without naming an actor, victim or technique; Mitel's advisory, revised to version 2.0 on 2026-11-24, now lists the CVE ids and makes no exploitation statement. Accenture APEX Labs reports that the AWV flaws were exploited before Mitel's advisory and patch: web-shell activity at one victim before 23:00 UTC on 2026-11-15, root within about 30 minutes, directory credentials recovered from MiCollab's LDAP configuration and used against a domain controller, local logs edited, and a second organisation's server talking to the same actor since 2026-11-09. A patched server cannot be assumed clean.

alerts.headline: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
alerts.summary: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-11-17 fix CVE-2026-114938, an out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder that Calif, one of its two credited reporters, scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and says it turned into pre-authentication code execution in the default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; Oracle scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity. Only x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI are affected, a trigger proof of concept is public, Calif withholds its product chains, a second researcher claims a working exploit with no release stated, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts without a confirmed success against its sensors, and VulnCheck says a working exploit is available to its customers. NCSC.ch and BACS warn operators to update internet-reachable Java applications and identity services first, and Cisco's advisory, at version 1.4, lists Catalyst Center, IOS XE and ISE as not affected while Siemens lists Siveillance Control, Siveillance Control Pro and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual with no fix yet.

updates.summary: GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-114938 as of 2026-11-18, none confirmed successful against its sensors, and VulnCheck says a working RCE exploit is available to its customers; Cisco lists 13 products as affected with fixed releases still to be determined, Fortinet is still investigating, BACS's warning adds internal systems and supplier clarification, and Tenable says Red Hat and Ubuntu had released no fix and Debian only an unstable-branch fix as of 2026-11-18, with Keycloak recommending a JVM option as the interim mitigation.

alerts.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE flaws, Strict mode does not remove them; France blames IRGC
alerts.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores, and on 2026-11-09 France's foreign ministry attributed that campaign, and only that campaign, to the Iranian unit Shahid Kaveh. More followed: more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops on 2026-11-02, altered cold-room settings at three sites of the French blood service through a supplier, and, per SRF on 2026-11-05, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores in Switzerland. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. On 2026-11-11 Midnight Blue reported six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, and on 2026-11-20 Danfoss published CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in an announced 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient, so removing internet exposure comes first, and BACS's statement of 2026-11-10 that updates fix the known flaws predates the report and does not cover the six. CISA added three older AK-SM 800A flaws (CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915 and CVE-2025-41450) to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without tying them to this campaign.

updates.summary: CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units. Blick reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores and sees no sign they were targeted.

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

CERT-FR's alert has a third version dated 2026-10-16 whose guidance differs for compromised and uncompromised units: the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, is to be checked, and a compromised Danfoss unit is to be restarted or otherwise factory-reset and reconfigured, with a caution to check insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink. The Dixell France operator guide that the alert links says any XWEB PRO on firmware 1.12.1 or earlier must be updated without delay, that XWEB units ship with a factory Admin account, and that remote access must go through an encrypted VPN; neither document names an entry vector.

The Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links was replaced on 2026-10-18 and now carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October 2026, which acknowledges the vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once, gives a restore procedure and says to check product temperatures in the cabinets directly; the earlier statements about XWEB PRO firmware 1.12.1, a CISA advisory and a March 2024 bulletin are no longer on that page and are removed. Le Monde's report that the defrost operation was lengthened from one hour to eight so that alarms trigger late, and SecurityWeek's figure of about 700 supermarkets, the prosecutor's report of fires and the absence of a claim or ransom demand, are added, with Cybersecurity Dive's report that Copeland confirmed the flaw was found in discontinued controllers.

ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, not vulnerabilities researchers had published, so a firmware update alone does not close the exposure. Forescout, on 2026-10-22, counts 12,976 exposed service observations in 99 countries, 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1, and over 20 hacktivist-claimed refrigeration attacks since January 2026, and says the French access vector remains unconfirmed.

Reuters reports that the Pentagon treats late-August freezer failures at at least six US military commissaries as a suspected hack, with Cyber Command and Army investigators in touch with their French counterparts, and Nextgov adds that two people familiar with the matter say US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers; neither says how the intruders got in, and no official has attributed the activity on the record.

The attacks returned on 2026-11-02 across Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia, and Finland per The Guardian: BleepingComputer counts more than 115 stores and says it is unclear whether the attacks were coordinated, Sabcobel says its sites were hit through the same vulnerability as in France, Euronews names Danfoss as the software supplier in both incidents while CyberInsider says the manufacturer and access method of the new wave remain unknown, and Coop Switzerland says attempts against it failed.

The attacks reached Germany: heise reports an Edeka market in Reisbach whose cooling systems were heated to 50 degrees overnight into 2 November, WDR quotes a CAP supermarket manager saying the attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely and reports that Rewe's head office confirmed an attack aimed at Danfoss; SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established; and Le Canard enchaîné reports that cold rooms of a contractor of the French blood service were programmed to 110 degrees overnight on 1 to 2 November, with no source tying that case to these controllers.

The French blood service EFS confirmed that an incident at its refrigeration supplier on 2 November altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three of its sites, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, so the case no longer rests on Le Canard enchaîné alone; ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action, CSIRT Italia issued cold-chain measures, and no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers.

SRF reported on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases of the refrigeration attacks in Switzerland, a butcher in Köniz whose freezer reached 50 to 70 degrees and three Volg stores with changed cooling parameters; BACS has received one reportable notification about an attack on commercial refrigeration, and CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint fact sheet on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers that names no vendor, CVE or actor. No source names the controller make or the access route in the Swiss cases.

NCSC Switzerland updated its advisory on 2026-11-06 with the Swiss incidents, Copeland and Dixell XWEB and healthcare, a four-point checklist for refrigeration management systems across all relevant operations, supplier-managed equipment included, and the statement that the public information does not establish a common attack method or confirm exploitation of the Danfoss CVEs it lists. Ransom-ISAC published the event log of one internet-reachable Copeland XWEB Pro compromise (743 parameter writes in two administrator sessions, default credentials claimed without published evidence), and Unit 42 counts over 5,000 exposed devices across countries on 5 and 6 November and a falling count in France since October.

France's foreign ministry and the C4 crisis cell attributed the 11 to 12 October refrigeration-controller campaign to Iran on 2026-11-09, naming the Revolutionary Guard unit Shahid Kaveh, and the Paris prosecutor requested arrest warrants against its leader and two deputies; the French documents cover that campaign only, and the later waves and the Swiss cases are not attributed in them.

BACS published its own public warning on 2026-11-10: it says Switzerland is affected and that the controllers also run in butchers, restaurants, pharmacies, doctors' practices, laboratories, logistics, industry and farms, many of whose operators do not know their plants are reachable from the internet, and it repeats that security updates for the AK-SM 800A and 8xxA family exist and that newer firmware enforces HTTPS.

Midnight Blue reported on 2026-11-11 six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, with no CVE identifier, no fixed version and no known exploitation (BSI); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient and removing internet exposure comes first, and BSI will not rule out flaws in firmware 5.4.0 (heise).

Danfoss published CVE ids for two controller flaws: CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in a coming 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, documented default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix). BSI's version 1.1 warning reports exploitation attempts against two Copeland XWEB EVO flaws.
The early report that ANSSI had found a flaw in the vendor's software comes from a person close to the French Prime Minister, quoted by AFP; the campaign reached at least six more European countries.

CISA added two 2023 Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws, CVE-2023-25914 (file read through the XML interface) and CVE-2023-25915 (command execution), and the 2025 authentication bypass CVE-2025-41450 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without naming a campaign; no source ties the listing to the refrigeration attacks. The 2023 flaws are fixed in software 3.3, and CISA's advisory for CVE-2026-129713 says no known public exploitation specifically targeting that vulnerability has been reported to it.

alerts.headline: N-central: Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and blocks the Legacy API; 4EverAble2Shell exploited; upgrade Agents too
alerts.summary: An independent researcher published proof-of-concept code on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 for what Huntress counts as 33 critical flaws in N-able's N-central appliance, and a second disclosure on 2026-11-12 added 4EverAble2Shell, a chain through Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436) that works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers, and Agent2Shell, SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints. Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26, 2026-11-10) fixed seven CVE ids and Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16) fixes 17 more, hardens how Agents and Probes authenticate and blocks the Legacy API permanently, but N-able does not name either chain or say it is fixed; Huntress reports public proof-of-concept code for all 17 and no exploitation of them in its partners' environments. Every on-premises server and every Agent and Probe must be on Hotfix 3, including those already on Hotfix 2.

updates.summary: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26) on 2026-11-10 with seven CVE ids, which replaces the entry's statements that no fix, no CVE ids and no affected or fixed builds existed, and reports scanning activity associated with the public proof-of-concept code but no evidence of successful exploitation; on-premises servers must be upgraded and every Agent and Probe upgraded too.

The researcher's second exploit set, 4EverAble2Shell, chains Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 with a root escalation, works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers per Huntback, with attempts recorded on Previdian's honeypot; N-able has no fix yet and says it has seen no signs of compromise.

N-able confirmed via Huntress that Agent2Shell, the researcher's other chain set that gives an unauthenticated attacker SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints, also needs the non-default Legacy API, and N-able has published indicators of compromise for customers that have not disabled it; N-able still has no fix, and its earlier statement that it saw no signs of compromise predates the indicators.

N-able released Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16): 17 more CVE ids fixed, Agent and Probe authentication hardened, the Legacy API permanently blocked, and every Agent and Probe must be upgraded even from Hotfix 2. N-able does not say Hotfix 3 fixes 4EverAble2Shell or Agent2Shell, and Huntress reports public proof-of-concept code for all 17 ids.

CISA listed the Apache Axis flaw CVE-2026-90436 behind 4EverAble2Shell as exploited on 2026-11-18. N-able's remediation page reads agent impersonation more narrowly than Huntress reads Agent2Shell: it needs an existing foothold on an endpoint and yields only what an agent receives.

actions: Update every ScreenConnect technician host client and Access agent to 26.6.5 or later now, not only the server, because the vulnerable code runs on the technician's machine; where that waits, remove the TransferFiles permission from every role and session group (Administration > Security > Roles).

Treat any pre-26.6.5 client that shows a second, unfamiliar RMM tool or an unexplained ScreenConnect connection ID as compromised and reimage it rather than patching in place, because every Host that joined a session with an infected client can have received and run the same infection chain.

On every ScreenConnect server, read a copy of App_Data\\Session.db for guest-originated RanFiles or SentFiles events that overlap an open host connection, and on any hit isolate the technician's workstation and rotate every credential reachable from it (RMM, PSA, vault, customer admin accounts), because Huntress saw one workstation fully compromised nine seconds after its client ran a guest-pushed file.

alerts.headline: ScreenConnect clients before 26.6.5 run guest-pushed files unprompted; Huntress confirms exploitation against MSPs
alerts.summary: CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9) lets file-transfer actions inside an already-active ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote session run without the authorization or Host-confirmation step the product is meant to require; ConnectWise fixed it in 26.6.5 on 8 September. Huntress has confirmed exploitation against MSP technicians since October 2026, with attacker guests spraying run-file requests across 42 MSP servers. Earlier, from 20 August, Huntress saw rogue ScreenConnect clients that push their infection chain as an auto-run file transfer on every new connection, behaviour that matches the flaw, though Huntress does not tie those incidents to the CVE.

updates.summary: Huntress confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians: on 2026-11-12 a guest-pushed batch file ran on a technician's client with no prompt and installed a rogue ScreenConnect client within about nine seconds, while attacker guests were making 688,000 run-file requests on 42 MSP servers between 2026-10-20 and 2026-11-16. Updating the server does not fix it; every technician host client must be on 26.6.5 or later.

Huntress does not tie its 20 August rogue-client incidents to CVE-2026-84869; the exploitation of the flaw it confirms runs from October 2026. The worm-like spread runs from an infected client to every Host that joins a session with it, not the other way round.

actions: Upgrade every clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier has no fix and must migrate) and, until it is in, limit TCP 4371 to 4372 to the cluster peers' addresses as F6 advises, because CISA lists CVE-2026-76466 as exploited and F6 saw two internet-reachable nodes compromised soon after a public proof of concept appeared.

alerts.headline: Cisco Expressway root RCE is exploited (CISA KEV, F6 incident): upgrade clustered units to X15.5.20 and check them
alerts.summary: Cisco's disclosure of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 3.1 9.8), which lets an unauthenticated attacker who holds persistent cookies run operating-system commands as root on Expressway-C and Expressway-E configured in a cluster; X15.5.3 and earlier get X15.5.20, X14 and earlier must migrate, and there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that, soon after a public proof of concept appeared, attackers compromised two internet-reachable X15.5.3 devices, reached two internal cluster nodes through one and ran Python scripts for scanning and credential theft, while Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. The same-day hardening releases for the Unified CM family and Unity Connection (up to 9.8, fixed in 15SU5) and for Snort 3 (9.0) are not known to be exploited.

updates.summary: CISA listed CVE-2026-76466 as exploited on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that soon after a public proof of concept appeared attackers compromised two internet-reachable Expressway X15.5.3 devices, then two internal cluster nodes, with root used for scanning and credential theft; Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. Priority moves to high.

Cisco gives two separate causes for CVE-2026-76466: persistent cookies, and client certificates that go unvalidated when TLS Verify Mode is enabled for clustering; it does not say clustering is what uses the cookies.

actions: Run contentscannerstatus on every Cisco Secure Email Gateway that has File Reputation enabled in a mail policy and update Content Scanner Tools to 25.3.0.5525 or later with contentscannerupdate wherever automatic updates are off; the update needs no restart.

On every such gateway, and on each member of a cluster, run grep "System Security" system_logs now: on a suspected-compromise message keep the forensic data before upgrading, then follow Cisco's recovery steps (a new virtual machine on a fixed release with a fresh configuration and renewed credentials for a virtual appliance, Cisco TAC for a physical one) for every member of that cluster.

alerts.headline: Cisco's mail gateway has a second exploited root flaw in four weeks; the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update

immediate_action.action: An unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through a gateway with File Reputation enabled gets root, Cisco confirms exploitation, and no workaround exists. Update Content Scanner Tools (no restart) on every gateway that has automatic updates disabled, then check system_logs on every cluster member for Cisco's "System Security" messages; Cisco strongly recommends restoring a compromised appliance and every member of its cluster, because the cluster's SSH private keys could be accessed.
immediate_action.title: Verify Content Scanner Tools 25.3.0.5525 or later on every Cisco Secure Email Gateway and run Cisco's compromise check today

alerts.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, an arbitrary file write in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools earlier than 25.3.0.5525 are exposed; there is no workaround, and the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update that needs no restart or upgrade, and in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780; a public Metasploit exploit module has existed since 2026-11-05.

updates.summary: A public Metasploit exploit module for CVE-2026-76519, merged on 2026-11-05 and listed in Rapid7's wrap-up of 2026-11-20, turns the flaw into a one-email path to root for anyone who runs it against a gateway with File Reputation enabled and Content Scanner Tools below 25.3.0.5525.
